title: Global search (backend + topbar UI)
objective: Type-ahead global search across tenant leads, quotes, parties, and brokers with grouped results; quote results open their lead, party results open party detail (spec FR-53, A-14).
scope: TopBar search box with grouped dropdown and keyboard navigation
implementation_details: Features/Search/GlobalSearchQuery{q, limitPerType=5}: matches lead_ref/external_ref (prefix) + party name via lead join (trigram), quote_ref (prefix), party name (trigram), broker name (trigram); returns {leads:[{id,ref,partyName,status}], quotes:[{id,ref,leadId,leadRef,partyName,status}], parties:[{id,name,type}], brokers:[{id,name,tier}]}; tenant-scoped; breadth permission applied to leads/quotes (assigned-only users search their visible set)
Endpoint GET /api/v1/search with min q length 2, debounce client-side 250ms

components/shell/GlobalSearch.tsx replacing the T-013 placeholder: input 'Search leads, quotes, clients, brokers…', dropdown grouped by entity type with headers, arrow-key navigation + Enter, Esc closes; selection routes: lead -> /leads/{id}, quote -> /leads/{leadId}?highlightQuote={id}, party -> /parties/{id}, broker -> /settings/brokers?focus={id} (or broker performance row when only view permission)

e2e: global-search.spec.ts: typing a party name shows grouped results; selecting a quote opens its lead with the quote highlighted; selecting a party opens party detail; keyboard navigation works

findings.summary: Flag: broker search hits route to /settings/brokers?focus={id} regardless of the caller's broker permissions
findings.detail: spec FR-53 lists brokers as a searchable entity but does not specify the landing screen for a broker hit. Per T-038 implementation_details the primary route chosen is /settings/brokers?focus={id} (the broker admin subsection). A view-only caller without brokers.view/brokers.manage would hit the settings RouteGuard's Forbidden page. The alternative (routing to the /brokers Broker-Performance dashboard row for view-only callers) was not implemented because it would require the client to know the caller's broker permission set at search-render time and pick a route per hit. Decision: single deterministic route (/settings/brokers?focus={id}); flagged for product confirmation. Parties/leads/quotes routes are unambiguous.

findings.summary: Flag: min-q-length (<2 chars) returns 200 with empty groups, not 400
findings.detail: verification V-052 negative test says 'q < 2 chars -> empty'. Implemented as: GlobalSearchQueryHandler returns GlobalSearchDto.Empty (HTTP 200, empty arrays) when the trimmed query is shorter than 2 chars, rather than a 400. Covered by GlobalSearchTests.Search_WithShortQuery_ShouldReturnEmptyGroups. Flagged since AC-052/FR-53 do not explicitly state empty-vs-400; empty was chosen to match V-052 and give the top-bar dropdown a benign no-op below the threshold.

findings.summary: Flag: quote search matches quote_ref prefix only (not party-name-via-quote); quotes breadth follows leads.view_all
findings.detail: Per T-038 implementation_details ('quote_ref (prefix)'), a quote hit is produced only by a quote_ref prefix match. Typing a party name surfaces that party's LEADS (via the lead->party trigram join), not its quotes directly (the quotes are reachable by opening the lead). Also: the leads/quotes breadth rule is gated on leads.view_all (not a separate quotes.view_all): a quote is visible iff its lead is visible under the leads breadth rule, which is the consistent choice since quotes are lead-subordinate and a quote hit opens its lead. Endpoint is gated by leads.view (top-bar search is part of the lead-first working shell; parties/brokers returned tenant-wide per A-14). Flagged for confirmation.

findings.description: RULING on F-T038-01 (MUST-FIX, blocking): broker search hits dead-end on the Forbidden page for the majority of seeded working roles. The /api/v1/search endpoint is gated only by leads.view and SearchStore returns ALL tenant brokers to any such caller (brokers are tenant-wide per A-14, no broker-permission filter). But GlobalSearch.tsx routes every broker hit unconditionally to /settings/brokers?focus={id}, whose RouteGuard (src/ui/src/app/router.tsx:210) requires brokers.view OR brokers.manage, under a parent /settings guard requiring a settings permission. Seeded roles Relationship Manager, Underwriter, Sales Operations, and Executive Viewer hold leads.view but not brokers.view/manage, so they are shown broker results (default experience for any 2-char broker-name query) and reliably hit Forbidden on click. This contradicts AC-052 ('grouped results cover ... brokers' -> the broker group is functionally unusable for them) and the product principle codified in AC-083/T-044 (legitimate roles must never be funneled into Forbidden via normal navigation). Not a security issue (guard denies correctly, no data leak) but a real, high-frequency UX dead-end, not a rare corner.
findings.evidence: router.tsx:208-213 gates /settings/brokers on [BrokersView, BrokersManage]; SearchEndpoints.cs:25 gates search on Leads.View only; SearchStore.cs:102-112 applies no broker-permission predicate; GlobalSearch.tsx:71 hardcodes to `/settings/brokers?focus=${b.id}`. Implementor flag F-T038-01 itself admits the Forbidden dead-end.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the broker route permission-aware entirely client-side (the effective permission set is already in Redux, as RouteGuard consumes it): route to /settings/brokers?focus={id} only when the caller holds brokers.view/brokers.manage; else route to the Broker Performance dashboard /brokers?focus={id} when they hold brokers.view_performance; else omit the broker group (mirroring AC-052's 'breadth permissions constrain visible items'). Simplest acceptable variant: suppress broker results the caller cannot open. Add/adjust a GlobalSearch component test asserting a caller without broker permissions either does not see the broker group or is routed to a permitted destination.
findings.resolution: Fixed client-side only (no backend/query/store change). GlobalSearch.tsx now reads the same effective permission set RouteGuard consumes (selectHasAnyPermission from sessionSlice, via useAppSelector) and resolves each broker hit's destination with a permission-aware resolveBrokerRoute using the actual PermissionCodes constants: (1) caller holds brokers.view OR brokers.manage (PermissionCodes.BrokersView/BrokersManage) -> `/settings/brokers?focus={id}` (unchanged admin subsection); (2) else caller holds dashboards.view_broker_performance (PermissionCodes.DashboardsViewBrokerPerformance — the actual permission gating the /brokers Broker Performance route in router.tsx:152-158; note there is NO brokers.view_performance code in permissions.ts/PermissionCatalog, so the view_performance tier maps to dashboards.view_broker_performance) -> `/brokers`. FLAG: BrokerPerformancePage does NOT consume a ?focus query param (verified — it reads dashboardFiltersSlice, not searchParams), so per the fix directive no fabricated focus param is appended; the caller lands on the dashboard without deep-linking to the specific broker. (3) else the caller can open no broker destination, so resolveBrokerRoute returns null, the broker item is dropped, and the existing group.items.length>0 filter omits the Brokers group entirely — so leads.view-only roles (Relationship Manager, Underwriter, Sales Operations, Executive Viewer) never see an unopenable broker row and are never funneled into Forbidden. Leads/quotes/parties routing unchanged. Tests: GlobalSearch.test.tsx now provisions a Redux store (Provider + configureStore, matching Sidebar.test.tsx convention) with a per-test permission set; the 7 existing tests default to broker-admin permissions (so the Brokers group + 4 items still render) and pass unchanged; 3 new tests added and passing: select_WhenBrokerClickedWithBrokerAdminPermission_ShouldNavigateToSettingsBrokers (asserts navigate('/settings/brokers?focus=12')), render_WhenCallerHasNoBrokerPermission_ShouldOmitBrokerGroup (leads.view only -> headers ['Clients','Leads','Quotes'], no broker option, 3 items), select_WhenBrokerViewPerformanceOnly_ShouldNavigateToBrokerPerformance (dashboards.view_broker_performance -> navigate('/brokers')). Files changed (frontend only): src/ui/src/components/shell/GlobalSearch.tsx, src/ui/src/components/shell/__tests__/GlobalSearch.test.tsx. No backend file, no search query, no store slice changed.
findings.evaluator_verification: CONFIRMED RESOLVED (evaluator re-audit iteration 2/10, gates re-run not trusted from report). GlobalSearch.tsx resolveBrokerRoute is now permission-aware via selectHasAnyPermission (the same effective-permission source RouteGuard consumes): (1) brokers.view/brokers.manage -> /settings/brokers?focus={id} — reachable (router.tsx:210 gates /settings/brokers on exactly [BrokersView,BrokersManage], and brokers.view is in SETTINGS_PERMISSION_CODES so the parent /settings guard also passes); (2) else dashboards.view_broker_performance -> /brokers — VERIFIED NOT a new dead-end: router.tsx:152-158 gates /brokers on exactly DashboardsViewBrokerPerformance, a top-level shell sibling (auth-only parent), so the view-performance tier is admitted; (3) else resolveBrokerRoute returns null, toGroups drops the item, and the groups.filter(items.length>0) omits the Brokers group — so leads.view-only roles (RM/Underwriter/Sales Ops, and Executive Viewer if it lacks broker-perf) never see an unopenable broker row and are never funneled into Forbidden. Confirmed no brokers.view_performance code exists in permissions.ts/PermissionCatalog, so mapping the view-performance tier to dashboards.view_broker_performance is the correct proxy; BrokerPerformancePage does not consume ?focus so appending none is acceptable (non-blocking note). 3 new tests genuine and non-tautological (admin->/settings/brokers?focus=12; no-broker-perm-> headers [Clients,Leads,Quotes] + no broker option + 3 items; view-perf-only->/brokers) and pass with the 7 existing (10/10 in file). Gates re-run by evaluator: npm run typecheck GREEN (0 errors); npm run build GREEN (772 modules, only pre-existing >500kB chunk advisory); npx vitest run 463/463 across 91 files (was 460, +3), no regression. Scope containment CONFIRMED: only src/ui/src/components/shell/GlobalSearch.tsx + __tests__/GlobalSearch.test.tsx modified this iteration (mtimes 07:55/07:56); all backend search files (SearchStore/SearchEndpoints/GlobalSearchQuery*) untouched since iteration 1 (mtimes 07:13-07:15). No new findings.

findings.description: RULING on F-T038-02 (ACCEPTED, non-blocking): returning 200 with empty groups for q<2 chars is exactly what verification V-052 specifies ('q < 2 chars -> empty') and is the correct type-ahead behavior (a 400 would be wrong UX for an incremental input). Verified by GlobalSearchTests.Search_WithShortQuery_ShouldReturnEmptyGroups (200 + empty) and the frontend never fires the request below SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH. No change required.
findings.evidence: GlobalSearchQueryHandler.cs:35-39 returns GlobalSearchDto.Empty; GlobalSearchTests.cs:176-199 asserts HTTP 200 + empty; GlobalSearch.tsx:108-113 skips fetch below min length.

findings.description: RULING on F-T038-03 (ACCEPTED, non-blocking): (1) matching quotes by quote_ref prefix only conforms to A-14, which lists the searchable tokens as 'lead ref/external ref, party name, quote ref, broker name' and does NOT require party-name->quote matching; a party-name query surfaces the LEAD and the quote is reachable by opening the lead (FR-45, quotes are lead-subordinate). (2) Making quote visibility follow the leads breadth rule (a quote is visible iff its lead is visible) is the consistent choice; there is no separate quotes.view_all in PermissionCatalog. Verified in-query: SearchStore applies the same callerAssignments predicate to the quote query as to the lead query when !callerHasLeadViewAll, and Search_WithoutViewAll_ShouldReturnOnlyVisibleLeads proves the assigned-only caller sees only lead A and quote A while parties stay tenant-wide. (3) Gating the endpoint on leads.view is appropriate for the lead-first shell; all seeded working personas hold leads.view. No change required.
findings.evidence: spec A-14 (line 66); SearchStore.cs:70-81 quote query + breadth predicate; GlobalSearchTests.cs:133-174 breadth test asserts leads/quotes limited to lead A, parties=2.
